history.summary: The Nepali Mandir on P.R. Hill in Kohima is a Hindu temple built in the Nepali pagoda style with multi-tiered timber roofs, serving the Nepali/Gorkha community of Kohima. Sources describe it as dedicated to various deities with carved wooden idols, but no source names the specific deities, gives a founding date, or lists festivals (all UNVERIFIED). Documentation is thin: the main descriptive source is an AI-generated heritage page (inheritage.foundation) plus a place listing; treat architectural and historical claims as unverified. Coordinates below come from a place listing and are approximate (verify). No verified photo of the actual temple was found, so media is empty.

name: Nepali Mandir, Kohima
town_description: Kohima is the capital of Nagaland, a hill city at about 1,444 m above sea level. It is famous for the 1944 Battle of Kohima and the Kohima War Cemetery, and hosts the annual Hornbill Festival at nearby Kisama. P.R. Hill is a locality within Kohima town where this Nepali-community temple stands.

travel.railway: Dimapur Railway Station, ~74 km by road; Kohima has no railway station (verify)
travel.road: Within Kohima town by taxi to P.R. Hill (verify)
